title: Neural crest cells

objective.text: Explain what neural crest cells are and why they matter so widely.

body.general: Which cells start at the fold edges, then roam the body? Cells along the edges of the neural folds break free from their neighbours [f1]. These neural crest cells become loose, mobile cells, called mesenchyme, and travel into the tissue below [f1,f6]. In the trunk they leave after the tube closes; in the head, before [f2]. Some settle under the skin and make pigment cells [f3]. Others form nerve clusters, nerve-wrapping cells and the inner adrenal gland [f8]. They build so much that they are called the fourth germ layer [f4].
body.mbbs: Neural crest cells arise at the crests (lateral edges) of the neural folds [f1]. They undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and migrate into the underlying mesoderm [f1]. Trunk crest leaves after neural tube closure; cranial crest leaves before closure [f2]. Trunk crest follows two routes [f3]. The dorsal route runs under the ectoderm and gives melanocytes [f3]. The ventral route passes through the cranial half of each somite [f8]. It gives sensory ganglia, sympathetic and enteric neurons, Schwann cells and adrenal medulla [f8]. Crest is ectoderm that makes mesenchyme, so mesenchyme is not the same as mesoderm [f6]. Crest is called the fourth germ layer [f4]. It takes part in at least a third of birth defects and in melanoma and neuroblastoma [f9].

facts.text: Cells at the crest (edge) of the neural folds let go of their neighbours, an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and migrate into the mesoderm below.
In the trunk, crest cells leave after the tube closes; in the head they leave before closure.
Trunk crest on the dorsal route travels under the skin and makes melanocytes.
Ventral-route trunk crest crosses the front half of each somite and makes sensory ganglia, sympathetic and enteric neurons, Schwann cells and adrenal medulla.
Crest cells build so many tissues that they are called the fourth germ layer.
Crest cells take part in at least a third of birth defects and in cancers such as melanoma and neuroblastoma.
Tier D: medium BMP at the plate–skin border, with FGF and WNT, switches on PAX3; SNAIL and FOXD3 then specify crest, and SLUG drives migration.
Tier D: high BMP gives epidermis, medium BMP gives crest, and very low BMP gives neural plate.
Neural crest is ectoderm, from the edge of the neuroectoderm, even though it makes mesenchyme; mesenchyme is not the same as mesoderm.
Crest cells build mostly peripheral and non-neural tissues, such as ganglia, melanocytes, face bones and adrenal medulla, not the brain or spinal cord.

misconceptions.wrong: Neural crest is part of the brain and spinal cord.
misconceptions.right: Crest cells leave the folds and build mostly peripheral and non-neural tissues: ganglia, melanocytes, face bones, adrenal medulla.

misconceptions.wrong: Neural crest is mesoderm because it makes bone and connective tissue.
misconceptions.right: It is ectoderm that makes mesenchyme; mesenchyme is not mesoderm.

checks.prompt: Neural crest cells come from which germ layer?
checks.why: Crest cells start at the edge of the neural folds, which are ectoderm; they make mesenchyme, not mesoderm.

checks.prompt: Which of these is made by neural crest cells?
checks.why: Trunk crest on the ventral route forms the adrenal medulla; the spinal cord comes from the neural tube itself.

checks.prompt: Trunk crest cells on the dorsal route, under the skin, become what?
checks.why: The dorsal route under the ectoderm gives pigment cells; the other choices come from the ventral route.

adult: Crest cells become pigment cells, sensory and autonomic ganglia, Schwann cells and the adrenal medulla [f3,f8].

remember.q: Where do neural crest cells come from?
remember.a: The edges of the neural folds, by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition [f1].

remember.q: Do trunk crest cells leave before or after the tube closes?
remember.a: After; head crest leaves before closure [f2].

remember.q: Why is the neural crest called the fourth germ layer?
remember.a: Because it builds so many different tissues [f4].
